newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS SUFFER FIRST LEAGUE DEFEAT OF SEASON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS SUFFER FIRST LEAGUE DEFEAT OF SEASON.

text.p: Vicenza halted Juventus's unbeaten league record with a 2-1 home win on Sunday which ruined the European Cup holders' chances of going top of serie A.

Defender Massimo Beghetto scored Vicenza's winner in the 71st minute after Ciro Ferrara appeared to have claimed a point for the visitors with a 47th-minute equaliser to Uruguayan Marcelo Otero's opening goal.
Juve finished the match with 10 men after midfielder Alessio Tacchinardi was sent for a crude tackle.

Inter, 2-0 winners over Piacenza on Saturday and now the only unbeaten club in serie A, lead the table with 11 points from five matches, a point ahead of four teams on 10 points -- Roma, who humiliated Milan 3-0 at the Olympic stadium on Saturday, Bologna, Parma and Juventus.
Davide Fontolan scored 20 seconds after the restart to set Bologna on their way to a 2-1 home win over Sampdoria.
Russian Igor Shalimov added a second before the visitors' late fightback was stemmed by the 82nd-minute dismissal of French midfielder Christian Karembeu -- for kicking Shalimov.
Enrico Chiesa scored Parma's winner in a fine 1-0 victory at Cagliari.
Oliver Bierhoff, hero of Germany's European championship triumph, struck a late equaliser for Udinese at Napoli before getting sent off for a foul on Brazilian sweeper Andre Cruz.
